record.title: One measured configuration approaches its instance maximum

aligned_passages.text: **Comparison with the same finite instance.** The concentration of the finite maximum in §11.1.2 strengthens this to a near-optimal sampled configuration. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is one finite deterministic word $W$, independent of $n$ and $J$, such that $$ \Pr_{J,\Sigma}\!\left\{ H_{n,J}(\Sigma)\ge\max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)-\varepsilon n \right\}\longrightarrow1. $$ To see this, choose the word with $v_W\ge P_*-\varepsilon/4$ and write $r_n=\mathbb E(E_n-v_W)^2\to0$ and $M_n=\max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)/n$. The convergence $\mathbb E M_n\to P_*$ makes its bias at most $\varepsilon/4$ for all sufficiently large $n$. ### 5.3 A fixed QAOA circuit before the thermodynamic limit Let $\widehat Z_i,\widehat X_i$ be Pauli operators, and define the cost and mixer by $$ C_{n,J}=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i0$ there is one finite $W$ with $v(W)\geq P_*-\varepsilon$, whose depth and angles depend on $\varepsilon$ but not on $n$ or $J$. The instance still determines $C_{n,J}$. Here depth counts global cost–mixer layers; their elementary gate counts depend on the implementation. This order of limits differs from the fixed-instance depth limit in [Farhi, Goldstone and Gutmann, §VI][FGG], which permits instance-dependent choices. The common-circuit conclusion was conjectured by [Basso, Farhi, Marwaha, Villalonga and Zhou (2022), §7, equation (7.2)][BFMVZ]. **The finite Gaussian input.** Fix the minimiser and its diffusion, a cutoff $0[long §7, “A finite Gaussian spin and its adjacent correlations”](../long/reasoning-record.md#finite-gaussian-approximation). **The rooted energy and its circuit realisation.** The next identity comes from a separate construction in [OpenAI (2026b), §2 and Lemma 3.1][Q]. Its classical sector consists of square-integrable functions built recursively from a local Gaussian seed and Gaussian coordinates generated by child functions; the inner product is expectation. Centred real child directions have lifts $\mathsf G(f)$ at the receiving root that form a centred Gaussian family with $$ \mathbb E[\mathsf G(f)\mathsf G(g)]=\langle f,g\rangle. $$ The receiving root's seed is independent of these coordinates. Compatible embeddings compare functions of different finite depths without changing earlier variables. The root shift $\mathsf L$ inserts a child direction into the first Gaussian chaos (the linear Gaussian part), with constant receiving-root state; its adjoint projects onto that part and returns the child direction. This representation builds on the fixed-depth spin–boson description of [Boulebnane et al. (2026)][spin-boson]. Start with the root seed $g_0$ and recursively put $Z_{j+1}=\mathsf G(g_j)$. The orthonormal child directions give independent standard Gaussian lifts, reproducing the scalar law. The finite spin $F_N$ depends only on those lifts. Projection therefore gives the exact rooted-energy identity $$ \begin{aligned} \mathsf L^*F_N&=\sum_{j=0}^N\mathbb E[F_NZ_{j+1}]g_j,\\ \mathcal E(F_N):=\operatorname{Re}\langle F_N,\mathsf L F_N\rangle &=\sum_{j=0}^N\mathbb E[F_Ng_j]\,\mathbb E[F_NZ_{j+1}] =S_{T,N}. \end{aligned} \tag{12} $$ Independence of the receiving-root seed removes the $j=0$ term. This identity concerns the finite Gaussian formula in a limiting rooted space, not a finite-$n$ circuit. The unshifted pairing can have the same scalar limit without identifying this energy. The construction and projection are proved in [long §8.1](../long/reasoning-record.md#rooted-energy). **Proposition 5 (circuit approximation; a consequence of [OpenAI (2026b), §§2–5][Q]).** For each fixed $T,N$ in the preceding construction with finite positive normalisers, and every $\eta>0$, there is a finite ordinary QAOA word $W$, with deterministic angles independent of $n$ and $J$, such that $$ |v(W)-S_{T,N}|<\eta. $$ This imports the circuit construction for these particular Gaussian data. Bounded smooth odd approximations to the transmitted functions, together with exclusions on dependencies between seed classes, make the formula eligible for Theorem 4.1 while changing its rooted energy arbitrarily little. Smoothing the final sign alone is insufficient. That theorem synthesises the formula with temporary Gaussian seed controls, reusing the same sitewise seeds throughout the word. Theorem 5.1 removes their joint effect using cost and mixer gates. Proposition 2.1 identifies the resulting fixed word's tree energy with $v(W)$. The absolute approximation bounds give Proposition 5; [long §§8.1–8.6](../long/reasoning-record.md#qaoa-construction) retain the eligibility conditions and proofs. The deduction of near-optimality is now explicit: $$ P_*-v(W)\leq (P_*-I_T)+|I_T-S_{T,N}|+|S_{T,N}-v(W)|. \tag{13} $$ Choose $T$ so that $1-T<\varepsilon/3$, then $N$ so that the second term is below $\varepsilon/3$, and finally use Proposition 5 with $\eta<\varepsilon/3$. These finite choices give $v(W)>P_*-\varepsilon$ before $n$ tends to infinity. The source's Appendix A supplies an alternative positive-temperature input to the same synthesis. The selected construction supplies no quantitative depth bound, finite-size rate or efficient procedure for finding angles. **Corollary 6 (a measured configuration on the same instance).** For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a finite ordinary QAOA word $W_\varepsilon$, chosen independently of $n$ and $J$, such that one computational-basis measurement $\Sigma$ satisfies $$ \Pr_{J,\Sigma}\!\left\{ \max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)-H_{n,J}(\Sigma)\leq\varepsilon n \right\}\longrightarrow1 \qquad(n\to\infty). \tag{14} $$ **Proof.** For a fixed word, put $Y_n=H_{n,J}(\Sigma)/n$ and $K_n=\max_\sigma H_{n,J}(\sigma)/n$. [Farhi, Goldstone, Gutmann and Zhou, §4, equations (13)–(22)][FGGZ] prove $$ \mathbb E_{J,\Sigma}Y_n\to v(W),\qquad \mathbb E_{J,\Sigma}Y_n^2\to v(W)^2. $$ The second moment is $\mathbb E_J\langle(C_{n,J}/n)^2\rangle$, so it includes measurement variance as well as disorder fluctuations. Thus $Y_n\to v(W)$ in joint $L^2$. Gaussian concentration of the maximum and its defining mean limit give $K_n\to P_*$ in probability. Choose $W$ with $P_*-v(W)<\varepsilon/3$. With probability tending to one, both $K_n-P_*<\varepsilon/3$ and $v(W)-Y_n<\varepsilon/3$, which proves (14). The two energies use the same $J$; no independence between them is needed. The companion's [§11.2, “What is averaged, and a fixed-word probability consequence”](../long/reasoning-record.md#fixed-word-probability) gives the concentration argument and its further probability consequences.
